 Judgment
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim
petitioners in O.P.(Mv) No.1814/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Perumbavoor
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 24/06/2019
. The sole respondent herein is the 3 rd respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.
2. The claimants are the wife and minor children of deceased Varghese.

According to the claimants,
on 04/12/2016 at about 08:00 a.m., Varghese was driving autorickshaw bearing registration number KL-41/C-2675 along the Angamaly- Chalakudy NH road and when he reached near the place by 2025:KER:40042 name Elavoor Kavala, KSRTC bus bearing registration number KL-15/A-1014 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner collided with the autorickshaw.
In the incident, Varghese sustained grievous injuries, to which he succumbed.
3. The 1st respondent in the original petition is the Managing Director, KSRTC and the 2 nd respondent, the driver of the offending bus.
4. The 3rd respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
The amount claimed was disputed.
It was also contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

6. The Tribunal on a consideration of the documentary 2025:KER:40042 evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the 2nd respondent driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 16,16,000/- together with interest @ 8%
per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioners have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides.
9.
The award of compensation under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioners - Notional income
The incident in this case took place on 04.12.2016.
According to the claim petitioners, the deceased was the driver as well as the owner of the autorickshaw he was driving at the time of the incident.
An amount of 30,000/- was claimed to be 2025:KER:40042 the monthly income of the deceased.
The Tribunal fixed the notional income of the deceased at 10,000/-.

This is challenged by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners who submitted that in the light of the dictum laid down in Manusha Sreekumar and Others v. United India Insurance Co.Ltd., 2022 KHC 7106 : AIR 2022 SC 5161, the notional income fixed by the Tribunal is quite low and that the monthly income ought to be fixed at 15,600/-.

entities.text: Manusha Sreekumar and Others v. United India Insurance Co.Ltd., 2022 KHC 7106 : AIR 2022 SC 5161
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This submission made by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners is opposed by the learned senior counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent insurer, who submitted that in the absence of any cogent evidence, the amount awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
The incident in Manusha Sreekumar (Supra) took place on 21/02/2015.
The deceased therein was a fish vendor cum driver.
Various documents were produced before the Tribunal to prove the claim that he was earning 25,000/- per month.

A course certificate showing that the deceased had completed 2 years course in electronic mechanic trade; a job training 2025:KER:40042 certificate;
his passport showing that he was employed in Oman for a period of about 4 years; a job offer from the UK offering the position of a Telecom Rigger; his bank statements and certificate of the Kerala Motor Transport Workers Welfare Fund Board. The Apex Court found that the deceased was a self employed man who donned multiple hats so as to provide a comfortable living for his family.

entities.text: Kerala Motor Transport Workers Welfare Fund Board
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It was in the light of the aforesaid evidence and also taking into account the fact that the deceased being a registered transport motor driver coming under the definition of driver as defined under the Kerala Fair Wages Act, 1971 his income was fixed in terms of notification G.O(MS) No.123/2015/LBR dated 04/09/2015.

In the case on hand, apart from Ext.A9 driving licence which shows that the deceased was authorised to drive vehicle including heavy goods motor vehicles with badge, there is no other evidence to support the claim that he was earning 30,000/- per month.
Nevertheless the amount of 10,000/- fixed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

Hence I find that the 2025:KER:40042 Bindhu Varghese vs The New India Assurance Company Limited on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196763509/
3 notional income of the deceased can be fixed at 13,000/-.

sentences.text: Loss of love and affection

The learned senior counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent-insurer draws my attention to the impugned award by which the Tribunal, in addition to loss of consortium, an amount of 50,000/- has been awarded as compensation towards loss of love and affection.

In the light of the dictums in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram, (2018) 18 SCC 130 : 2018 KHC 6697, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur, AIR 2020 SC 3076 : 2023 KHC 760 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Somwati, 2020 KHC 6530 : (2020) 9 SCC 644, the compensation that has been awarded by the Tribunal for 'loss of love and affection' as well as loss of consortium is apparently incorrect.

In the result, the appeal is allowed in part by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 3,69,944/- (total compensation 19,85,944/- that is, 16,16,000/- granted by the Tribunal +
3,69,944/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the delay of 38 days in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The 3rd respondent/insurance company is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of 2025:KER:40042 the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claimants/appellants at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
